newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST GRAIN FUTURES MKT WAVERS AFTER SLOW WEEK.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST GRAIN FUTURES MKT WAVERS AFTER SLOW WEEK.

text.p: The grain futures market of the Budapest Commodity Exchange remained hesitant after a week of below-average turnover and was unlikely to reactivate until developments expected for mid or late March, traders said.
"Wheat crop estimates are not expected until late March, while existing excess maize stocks (of over one million tonnes) have yet to find their way to the market," said Istvan Grebats of Termin.
Growers are reluctant to sell on the spot market at current, already depressed prices but will eventually be forced to do so as they will have to finance spring field work.
Maize futures remained mostly steady, except for March which ended at 19,060 forints, down 130, and May which finished at 18,450, down 50.
Milling wheat prices ended lower for five maturities, rose for one and remained steady for two, with July and August moving in opposite directions.
"This was due to a major player buying July and selling August," Grebats said.
Blackseed prices dropped 200 forints for December and 400 for November, to end at 42,400 and 42,000 forints respectively.
"The futures market started to incorporate the new bonus system in prices," Grebats said.

Hungary will introduce a progressive bonus in the blackseed acquisition system from this autumn's crop and the minimum required oil percentage of 44 percent -- where the bonus starts -- is reasonably easy to reach, Grebats said.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
